text:
amal: Heads up — security-bot just alerted about stale cross-account KMS grants tied to our snapshot pipeline. Looks like grants created by the `snapshot-uploader` role weren’t revoked after the CMK rotation.

security-bot: [ALERT] KMS_GRANT_STALE for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345 - grantId 9a8b7c6d created_by snapshot-uploader. Created: 2025-11-02T14:12:03Z, rotation_time: 2025-12-01T00:00:00Z, last_seen: 2026-02-10T09:21:00Z.

jason: Ugh. Do we know whether the grant was ever used post-rotation or just left around?

amal: CloudTrail shows a few S3:GetObject calls using that grant on 2026-02-10. I pulled the snippet: 
```
2026-02-10T09:20:59Z s3.amazonaws.com GetObject Key=snapshots/db-20260210.tar.gz principalId=arn:aws:sts::210987654321:assumed-role/external-consumer/session123 encryptionContext={kms_key_id=abcd-ef01-2345} requestID=...
```

sara: So external consumer still pulling snapshots. Could be legitimate, or stale long-lived creds. We need to triage: (1) revoke the grant, (2) check who created it + why, (3) ensure restoreability for affected snapshots.

ops-oncall: On it. Running `aws kms list-grants` to enumerate. Will post output if anything weird.

ops-oncall: ```
$ aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-ef01-2345 --region us-west-2
Grants:
- GrantId: 9a8b7c6d, GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/snapshot-uploader, RetiringPrincipal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rotation-agent, CreationDate: 2025-11-02T14:12:03Z
- GrantId: e1f2d3c4, GranteePrincipal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/internal-service, CreationDate: 2026-01-05T10:00:00Z
```

kevin: That first grant is cross-account (2109...), looks like a partner consumer. Was that an intended long-term grant? I thought we scoped snapshot access via temporary pre-signed URLs or short-lived STS sessions.

maria: I searched infra tickets. There was a one-off onboarding in 2025-11 where we granted snapshot access to partner A for a migration window. The ticket suggested revoking after 30 days but someone missed it.

amal: Okay immediate plan: revoke the stale grant for partner A, rotate any long-lived creds tied to that partner, and run a snapshot restore test from the preserved backup copies to ensure we don't break restores. Anyone object?

jason: No objections. Two quick asks: (a) before revoke, confirm last-used timestamp so we can notify partner and (b) check whether any automation creates grants on rotation — we might have a race where rotation script re-creates grants.

ops-oncall: Got you. Querying CloudTrail for KMS CreateGrant / RevokeGrant events and matching by grantId.

ops-oncall: ```
$ aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=abcd-ef01-2345 --max-results 50
Events:
- CreateGrant grantId=9a8b7c6d user=svc-snapshot-admin time=2025-11-02T14:12:03Z
- CreateGrant grantId=e1f2d3c4 user=rotation-agent time=2026-01-05T10:00:01Z
- (no RevokeGrant for 9a8b7c6d)
```

sara: That matches the missed-revoke hypothesis. amal can we notify partner support before we revoke? We should schedule a short maintenance window and confirm they have an alternative ingress.

amal: I'll ping them. But for risk containment I want a targeted revoke now and we can re-grant an auditable short-lived alternative if they need it.

ops-oncall: Revoking now: `aws kms revoke-grant --key-id abcd-ef01-2345 --grant-id 9a8b7c6d --region us-west-2`

ops-oncall: ```
> aws kms revoke-grant --key-id abcd-ef01-2345 --grant-id 9a8b7c6d --region us-west-2
{
  "ResponseMetadata": {
    "RequestId": "req-0a1b2c3d4e",
    "HTTPStatusCode": 200
  }
}
```

maria: Confirmed CloudTrail now logs RevokeGrant for that grantId. Also found associated service account `svc-legacy-onboard` that created it. Ticket created: INFRA-4123 to rotate that account's creds and audit other grants it created.

kevin: For longer-term: we should disallow cross-account long-lived grants by policy and force all partner access through a short-lived proxy pattern. Also add an automated lambda to revoke grants older than X days unless flagged.

jason: Agree. Also add a post-rotation check in the rotation pipeline: after CMK rotate, call `list-grants` and validate no unexpected cross-account grants exist; fail the rotation if policy violation detected.

amal: Action items: 
- amal: notify partner support + schedule maintenance (ETA 30m)
- ops-oncall: run restore tests from snapshots with new key state and confirm integrity (ETA 1h)
- kevin: draft RBAC policy change to forbid grant creation for non-approved roles (ETA EOD)
- jason: add rotation pipeline validation (PR plan)
- sara: update incident playbook and add automated CloudTrail alert rule (ETA tomorrow)

ops-oncall: Restore test started: `./tools/restore_snapshot.sh s3://redwood-snapshots/db-20260210.tar.gz --kms-key abcd-ef01-2345`

ops-oncall: ```
> ./tools/restore_snapshot.sh s3://redwood-snapshots/db-20260210.tar.gz --kms-key abcd-ef01-2345
Fetching object... OK
Decrypting with KMS key abcd-ef01-2345... OK
Extracting... OK
Start DB import... OK
Import completed, sanity checks passed.
```

maria: Good — restores succeed. That reduces blast radius. We'll still re-encrypt any exported snapshot copies if we rotate the CMK again.

kevin: Also logging recommendation: include grantId and creator principal in all snapshot access logs we emit to our own audit index, make it searchable so post-mortems are faster.

amal: Filing follow-ups: INFRA-4123 (rotate svc-legacy-onboard & audit), SEC-4390 (policy to prevent cross-account long-lived grants), DEVEX-221 (rotation pipeline check). I'll add a short after-action note to weekly all-hands.

jason: Nice triage. :thumbsup:

security-bot: [INFO] Incident record created SEC-4390; automated check scheduled daily for grants older than 30 days.

amal: Closing thread for now — will reopen if partner reports an issue. Thanks everyone.
